Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff
Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff

Pride and Progress News-highlights: 1. The AIDS-centered play "The Normal Heart" banned from performing at Washington D.C.'s Kennedy Center after the Supreme Court ruling on the Georgia sodomy laws 2. Man sues the San Diego Police Dept. for arresting him at their Gay Pride Parade and forcibly administering the HTLVIII antibody test 3. Urvashi Vaid becomes the Information Director of the National Gay and Lesbian Task Force 4. Officer court-martialed for refusing to submit to testing for the HTLVIII antibody COMMERCIAL: Urban General Warehouse Sale 5. Iowa's Democratic Party Convention refuses to change the state constitution to give gays a vote on the central committee 6. Andy Humm on courage COMMERCIAL: "First Hand" gay magazine 7. Chicago judge vacates court order for gay fathers to have to take the HTLVIII antibody test before being allowed to have custody of their children 8. Introduction of laws for the regulation of "poppers" as a recreational drug 9. Ability of men to get pregnant by implanting a fertilized egg in the anus COMMERCIAL: "New York Native" with Quentin Crisp 10. Sports Report 11. Outreach: Conversations with GMHC: Second part of the interview with Bruce Patterson and Scott Jordan, discussing relationships as a person with AIDS 12. Closing credits
The Right Stuff: 1. The Fabulous Follies: Drag star Hurricane Sommers lip-synchs to Patti Labelle's song "Oh" over clips of NYC's Gay Pride Parade COMMERCIAL: "Manscape" magazine 2. Newsweek magazine coverage, discussion of NYC AIDS doctor and homosexual abuse by a Massachusetts college president 3. Channel 5's coverage of the Georgia sodomy laws, with clips 4. Rate of AIDS in Haiti among straight men and women very high COMMERCIAL: Body Mate exercise equipment 5. Coverage of the rally race between Los Angeles and New York City COMMERCIAL: Waterfront Airways 6. Coverage of film "The Manhattan Project," starring John Lithgow and Cynthia Nixon 7. Closing credits
